title: U.S. House · Utah's 2nd District
area: Northern Utah under the congressional map first used in 2026, drawn by a Third District Court after the Legislature's 2021 map was struck down; largely overlaps the old 1st District, including Ogden and parts of Davis and Weber counties.

context.text: Utah's congressional map was redrawn for 2026 by court order in League of Women Voters v. Utah State Legislature. As a result, incumbent Blake Moore — who represented the old 1st District — is running for this newly drawn 2nd District rather than a district with the same boundaries he previously held. Moore defeated Karianne Lisonbee 56.7%-43.3% in the June 23, 2026 Republican primary.

candidates.name: Blake Moore
candidates.ballotNote: Defeated Karianne Lisonbee 56.7%-43.3% in the June 23, 2026 Republican primary
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative, Utah's 1st District (since 2021); Vice Chair of the House Republican Conference

priorities.text: Says he helped draft tax-cut legislation that doubled the child tax credit, ended taxes on tips, car-loan interest, Social Security benefits and overtime, and increased wages "by up to $7,200 per worker."
As co-chair of the House Air Force Caucus and House Depot Caucus, says he has worked to secure funding and infrastructure for Hill Air Force Base and Utah's defense workforce.
Says he prioritizes secure borders and a "lawful immigration system," and supports House Republican border security legislation.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Ways and Means (Health, Social Security, and Trade subcommittees) and the House Committee on Budget in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

candidates.researchNotes: Federal key floor votes and FEC finance totals for this sitting member of Congress are added separately by script; this entry focuses on stated positions, committee roles and sponsored priorities.

candidates.name: Peter Crosby
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Democratic primary without appearing on the ballot after the primary was canceled; also withdrew from the 1st District Democratic primary earlier in 2026

priorities.text: Affordability: housing costs, the cost of living and healthcare costs, and local jobs and small businesses.
priorities.quote: Confronting the housing crisis and the rising cost of living, including our healthcare costs, and standing up for the local jobs and small businesses that hold our towns together.

priorities.text: Accountability: a ban on congressional stock trades, a conversation on term limits, and removing corporate dark money from politics.
priorities.quote: Banning congressional stock trades, opening a real conversation on term limits, and getting corporate dark money out of our politics.

priorities.text: Stewardship: protecting public lands and restoring the Great Salt Lake.
priorities.quote: Protecting our public lands, restoring the Great Salt Lake, and standing up for communities against corporate developments

positions.summary: Says he would work with other members of Congress to end the Trump administration tariffs, which he describes as hurting local businesses.
positions.quote: I would join other willing members of Congress and bring an end to an illegal tariff regime that is making it harder and harder for our local business and entrepreneurs to make a living.

positions.summary: Says he prefers a single-payer system that allows private insurers to continue, and asks why Medicare should not be expanded to include more Americans.
positions.quote: Medicare, when well-funded and supported, works great for seniors. Why not expand this great program to include more Americans?

candidates.researchNotes: Positions, statements and priorities come from Crosby's campaign Policies page (petercrosbyforcongress.org/policies). The healthcare position was updated from the earlier budget-law quote to his single-payer statement. No stated positions found on abortion, guns, immigration or Israel. No campaign website content or detailed public policy statements were found beyond his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey and biographical facts.

statements.quote: Rewrite the current tax code so that large tech companies pay their fair share of taxes to support our government and communities.
I support regulatory reform for our housing markets

candidates.name: Carlton Bowen
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the April 10, 2026 Independent American Party of Utah convention
candidates.currentRole: State Chair, Independent American Party of Utah (self-described)

priorities.text: Says every vote he casts will begin with asking where the constitutional authority is for it.
priorities.quote: Every vote I cast in the U.S. House will begin with one question: Where is the Constitutional authority?

priorities.text: National debt: says he will not vote to increase the debt limit or for annual deficit spending unless Congress has declared war.
priorities.quote: I will not vote to increase the debt limit or for annual deficit spending unless Congress has declared war.

priorities.text: Opposes the Box Elder data center and says he would use constitutional powers available to a member of Congress to undo its approval.
priorities.quote: I oppose the Box Elder Data Center.

candidates.researchNotes: Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey and campaign website (bowenforcongress.com) reviewed. His stated priorities are the Constitution, the national debt and the Box Elder data center; he also opposes warrantless surveillance. None squarely takes a side on the guide's issue statements, so no positions or statements were added. He answered the Salt Lake Tribune questionnaire (Oct. 12, 2026) on debt, water and corruption. No campaign website content was found; biography draws on Ballotpedia and his 2026 Candidate Connection survey.

candidates.name: Daniel Cottam
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the April 18, 2026 Libertarian Party convention

priorities.text: Federal budget: says a congressman's responsibility is to pass a balanced budget (2024 survey).
priorities.quote: The responsibility of a congressman is to pass a balanced budget for the federal government.

priorities.text: Medicare reform: says he is not afraid to say Medicare needs reform (2024 survey).
priorities.quote: I am not afraid to say we need to reform Medicare.

priorities.text: Social Security: proposes raising the retirement age by at least three years with a gradual phase-in (2024 survey).
priorities.quote: we need to raise the retirement age by at least 3 years across the board with a gradual phase in.

candidates.researchNotes: No 2026 Candidate Connection survey, campaign website or Salt Lake Tribune questionnaire answers found. Statements and priorities come from his 2024 Ballotpedia survey from an earlier U.S. House campaign and may not reflect his current platform. No campaign website content or 2026 Candidate Connection survey was found; the survey cited here is from 2024.

statements.quote: I would also allow Medicare to negotiate with drug companies for drug prices.
statements.context: In his 2024 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey (2024 U.S. House campaign)

statements.quote: Until we accept the fact that the only way to solve the housing crisis is higher density we will continue to have relatively unaffordable housing.
statements.context: In his 2024 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey (2024 U.S. House campaign)

statements.quote: It means saying no when the president wants to get us involved in a foreign war without our consent.
statements.context: In his 2024 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey (2024 U.S. House campaign)

candidates.name: Robert Moesinger

priorities.text: Argues the core problem in American politics is the two-party system itself, which he says creates bad incentives for representatives; supports moving toward a multi-party system to increase voter choice and legislative independence.
priorities.quote: An election that sends a Republican or Democrat to their respective Washington trench fortifies the dominance and dysfunction of the two parties.

positions.summary: Says zoning reforms that allow more homes to be built are part of the answer to housing affordability.
positions.quote: encouraging zoning reforms that allow more homes to be built

candidates.researchNotes: Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey and Salt Lake Tribune candidate questionnaire (Oct. 12, 2026) reviewed. His campaign centers on ranked-choice voting and multi-member House districts; the housing answer is the only direct match to the guide's issue list.
